wolfram.note: Both decline on an empty collection: compute-engine answers Missing, Wolfram's Last[{}] stays unevaluated.
mathlib4.note: The last of an empty collection is Missing in compute-engine; the binding refuses it rather than defaulting, and the bare [] has no element type besides.

caption: A sum may be a list once its symbols are bound, so $Last(a + b)$ stays unevaluated
wolfram.note: An untyped symbol may be a list, so ours leaves Last(a + b) as it is; Wolfram reads the parts of the expression as written.

Last[1/b]: Wolfram's FullForm of 1/b is Power[b,-1], so Last gives -1 (the exponent). Our canonical form for division is a genuine Divide(1,b) with operands [1,b], so Last gives b. Both are internally consistent with their own canonical representation of division; structure-sensitive heads like Last necessarily disagree as a result. An untyped symbol may be a list, so ours leaves Last(1/b) as it is; Wolfram reads the parts of the expression as written.
